blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Fraser Valley

items.t: ALR vs non-ALR is the first split in every valley acreage trade: The structural profile that IS sourced: acreage housing in the ALR is freehold in practice and single-residence-led — one principal residence (≤500 m²) plus at most one additional residence (90 m² / 186 m² by parcel size), a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, and no stratification without ALC permission — so the multi-unit strata profile of urban pages does not exist on ALR parcels. A valley-wide ALR share of the acreage stock: unconfirmed — no official or permitted source publishes one.

Serviced vs unserviced is the second split: Built urban-fringe parcels sit on municipal water and sewer under their city's or township's servicing bylaw; rural and FVRD parcels trade on well and septic, with water licences and irrigation rights as separate parcel facts.

items.t: What the page is: a regional topic page titled "Fraser Valley Acreages for Sale | Rural Homes & Estates," whose editorial copy spans the Fraser Valley "from Langley to Chilliwack and beyond" and links out to Langley acreages, a farmland-buying guide, Fraser Valley farms, and South Surrey farms and acreage pages. It is not an area page and has no boundary of its own.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in Fraser Valley

items.t: Abbotsford frame (Abbotsford parcels only, for contrast): OCP Abbotsforward 2050 CURRENT; SSMUH bylaw number unconfirmed (never assert "3560-2024"); secondary suite capped under 50%; coach/garden suite 15% of lot area to a maximum 100 m² (Abbotsford only, never exported); taxes due July 2, 5% July 3, +5% September 16, 2026; Abbotsford HAS a Supreme Court registry. None of this applies to a Township, Surrey, Mission or FVRD parcel.

Mission / FVRD frames (each as its own): City of Mission — OCP 6405-2026 (adopted Apr 21, 2026); Zoning 5949-2020; SSMUH incorporation Bylaw 6299-2024 (unit counts unconfirmed); DSCB 5650-2017 (City source); FLAT 10% tax penalty after July 2 (Community Charter ss.233–234); NO Supreme Court registry (mapping unconfirmed). FVRD rural ground — Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11: taxes due July 2, 5% on amounts unpaid July 2 + further 5% on amounts unpaid October 31; notice from the Surveyor of Taxes, paid to the Province; FVRD bylaw numbers unconfirmed, never borrowed. A parcel's frame follows its jurisdiction, never its mailing address or its board sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fraser Valley

items.t: There is no acreage statistic to hide behind: Every community figure a buyer sees beside an acreage listing is a housing figure (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined) that contains the acreage without measuring it. Pricing an acreage parcel by parcel — on its own community's comparables, its ALR status, water, buildings and farm income — is not a preference in this market; it is the only method the permitted sources support.
The stratification sentence is the valley's most-misstated rule: The correct form is "cannot be stratified WITHOUT the ALC's permission" (Bulletin 09 s.6; ALCA s.21(1)) — a permission rule.

Servicing numbers do not travel: A buyer comparing a Township parcel (5382 CONFIRMED) with an FVRD parcel (numbers unconfirmed) and a Chilliwack parcel (candidate 3055 not adopted) is looking at three different evidentiary positions, not three numbers — the honest answer for the second and third is the process, and borrowing Mission's or Chilliwack's numbers for FVRD ground is expressly barred.

faq.q: Is there a published Fraser Valley acreage market statistic?
faq.a: No. SnapStats — the permitted source for this research — publishes no acreage segment: no acreage count, share or median exists for the Fraser Valley or any community in it. Acreages sit inside their own communities' ordinary Detached rows, split only as Detached vs Condos & Townhomes (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: How many homes can I have on an ALR acreage?
faq.a: Generally one principal residence (maximum 500 m² total floor area), plus, where the property qualifies, one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha; more than that, or a larger residence, requires ALC approval, and local bylaws may restrict further.

faq.q: Can I stratify or subdivide an ALR acreage into strata lots?
faq.a: Not without the ALC's permission: depositing a strata plan is a subdivision, and ALCA s. 21(1) bars subdividing agricultural land unless the Commission permits it or the ALR General Regulation allows it (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6).

faq.q: What farm income does an acreage need to keep farm classification?
faq.a: BC Assessment's minimum gross farm income (farm gate) thresholds are $2,500 for an operation of 0.8 ha to 4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation, and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha; new applications are due by the legislated October 31 deadline.

faq.q: Which communities does this page's feed cover?
faq.a: At reading, the visible cards were labelled with Langley sub-areas (County Line Glen Valley, Willoughby Heights, Campbell Valley, Salmon River, Otter District) and Abbotsford sub-areas (Abbotsford West, Poplar), at $1,699,000–$5,995,000 in card text — a regional feed, which is why no single community's statistics are presented as this page's figures.
